**Finding submitted: deviation (critical, ip-data).**

What I found in the IBM e-business Hosting Agreement:

- **§ 7(a) (p0082)** — all Materials delivered to us default to **Type II**, i.e. owned by IBM or third parties, unless the parties expressly agree otherwise. That means work product created for us during the Service performance period lands in IBM's hands by default, contrary to our position that we own what we pay for.
- **§ 7(c) (p0085)** — the Type II licence back to us is irrevocable/worldwide/paid-up but limited to use "within Customer's Enterprise only" with **no right to modify or prepare derivative works**, which falls short of even our fallback position.
- **No Customer Data / Content ownership statement anywhere.** Content and Customer Components are defined (p0017, p0019) and § 11.6 only makes us *responsible* for Content; § 14.17 confirms no rights arise beyond those expressly granted, so there is no affirmative confirmation that we retain title.
- Nothing assigns our IP or data to IBM and there is no joint ownership, so no walk-away trigger. IBM's ownership of the Base Components (§ 12.1) is acceptable.

Redline (validated ok:true): flip the § 7 default to **Type I** (Customer-owned), extend the Type II licence to be perpetual and to permit derivative works and use for the operation of our business, and add a new § 7(e) confirming we retain all right, title and interest in Content and Customer Components with no assignment to IBM and no joint ownership. Fallback offered in the comment if IBM will not move the default.
